surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Broberg sparks the Blues back from three down
paras: What a comeback. Kasperi Kapanen opened the scoring for the Oilers early in the first, and Leon Draisaitl extended the lead to 2-0 midway through the second, his 1,100th NHL point. Dalibor Dvorský got the Blues on the board late in the period. Filip Hållander scored his first goal for Edmonton 45 seconds later to make it 3-1 for the Oilers. The third period was a wild one. Colton Dach made it 4-1 early in the period. Philip Broberg, Pavel Buchnevich and Jimmy Snuggerud scored three goals in a little over five minutes midway through the period to tie it 4-4. Jake Neighbours and Mason McTavish scored in the shootout for the Blues.

The Oilers had a little more of the play and hit two posts and the crossbar, but the Blues won the shootout. Joel Hofer made 26 saves for the Blues, and Tristan Jarry stopped 23 of 27 at the other end. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Ryan Shea, even in a loss, by our Swing measure.
The Blues killed all four Oilers power plays. The Blues moved to 13-9-2 and climbed to fifth in the Central, while the Oilers fell to 17-5-4, still first in the Pacific.

items.text: Four straight wins for the Blues.
Connor McDavid extended his point streak against St. Louis to ten games.
The Oilers are winless in three (0-2-1).
Jimmy Snuggerud has a point in four straight games, with a goal in each of the last three.
